factProposals.value: A flagged script can be approved or rejected by a reviewer, and either decision is final. A script with missing parts can only be rejected. Scripts that were not flagged cannot be reviewed. Approving publishes nothing.

Reviewer decisions are stored in an append-only JSON-lines log at data/review_actions.jsonl with the script id, decision, typed reviewer name, note, a hash of the reviewed text and the time. There is one decision per script id. The script log keeps the status 'flagged' after a decision.
Reviewers use a command-line script that lists flagged scripts with their full text and flag reasons, records approve or reject, and prints a receipt. There is no web page.

A conflicting second decision is refused with an error naming who decided, an unreadable log raises an error instead of showing an empty list, and a script left as draft by a crash while flagging is recovered when the list is next read.
There is no login: the reviewer is a name typed on the command line and is not verified.

decisions.statement: Treat a script as uncertain when one of the existing STORY-002 review rules matches it; add no confidence score.
decisions.rationale: The generator is a stub and produces no confidence value.

decisions.statement: Make both approval and rejection final.
decisions.rationale: The project owner's choice for this story.

decisions.statement: Allow only rejection for a script with missing parts; other flag reasons can be approved by a reviewer.
An identical repeat decision changes nothing; any other second decision raises an error naming who decided and what.
decisions.rationale: The project owner asked that a conflicting decision is never dropped silently or reported as success.

decisions.statement: Keep reviewer decisions in their own log and leave the STORY-001 and STORY-002 files unchanged.
decisions.rationale: The project owner asked that earlier story files are not changed without asking.

decisions.statement: Recover a missing flag line by re-running the review checks on draft-only scripts when the queue is read.
decisions.rationale: The project owner chose this so a crash while flagging does not hide a script, without changing the pipeline.

limitations.statement: A rejected script cannot be replaced by a regenerated one with the same id: the new text can never be approved.
A script flagged only because the generator marked it approved (pre_approved) is not recovered after a crash while flagging; it stays out of the list until the pipeline is run again for that idea.
Crash recovery sees only the script's title and theme, not the idea's, so a blocked word that appears only in the idea would be missed if a generator changed them.
The typed reviewer name proves nothing about who decided.
One reviewer at a time: two decisions or listings made at the same moment are not protected against each other.
Listing and reviewing may write to the script log, because that is where a missing flag line is recovered.
Refused review attempts are not recorded; only accepted decisions are logged.
